aspiration_pool_note: 21 original programme-specific options + 8 new cluster-level, deliberately non-exclusive options added for Experiment 1 (e.g. 'Healthcare Professional (General)' maps to 6 programmes). Every one of the 21 trained programmes now has at least 2 aspiration options that can plausibly lead to it, fixing the exclusive 1:1 mapping the baseline flagged.

scoring_weights_in_label_assignment.note: assign_programme_label() and its scoring weights are UNCHANGED from the baseline - this experiment did not touch the labelling rule at all. What changed is upstream of it: which profiles get generated in the first place.

generation_change_summary.what_changed: Replaced the baseline's two-stage generator (a uniform-random draw for the bulk of the dataset, decoupled from any programme, plus a hand-picked 5-class-only biased top-up) with one mechanism applied to all 21 trained programmes: for every profile, a target programme is chosen first, then interests/skills/strengths are drawn with a weighted bias toward that programme's own associated tags (55-70% probability per pick) vs. a shared cross-cutting pool or the full pool otherwise, aspiration is drawn from that programme's now-non-exclusive aspiration list 75% of the time (else fully random), and KCSE grades are floor-enforced against the target's real KUCCPS minimums. The SAME assign_programme_label() rule then decides the actual label, which can and does differ from the target - nothing forces the outcome.
generation_change_summary.why_the_result_changed_this_much: Under the baseline generator, only 5 of 21 classes ever received programme-biased interests/skills/strengths; the other 16 classes' non-aspiration signals were pure noise relative to the label, leaving aspiration as close to the only usable signal for many classes. Every class now has real, multi-attribute correlated signal in its training data (the same correlation _score_programme already used to assign labels), which is why accuracy rose substantially without any change to the labelling rule or its weights.
generation_change_summary.leakage_check_performed: Per-class recall ranges 65%-97% (Software Engineering lowest, Journalism/Pharmacy highest) with no class at or near 100%, and Software Engineering's 71 misclassifications land 72% on Informatics & Computer Science (its documented confusable neighbour) and BBIT's land mostly on BCom/ICS (also documented neighbours) - see confusion_matrix.json. This is the expected signature of genuine, non-degenerate overlap between thematically similar programmes, not a new single-feature shortcut.

hyperparameter_search.method: GridSearchCV, 5-fold, scoring=f1_weighted, searched on 80% train split only
